title: Constructor chaining with defaults

blocks.text: **Constructor chaining**: write the most specific constructor first, and have the others call it with `this(...)`, so the defaults and the checks live in one place.

items: `Employee(String name, int id)`: the department is `General`;
`Employee(String name)`: the id is `0` and the department is `General`.

blocks.text: Every constructor refuses a name that is `null` or blank (only whitespace) with an `IllegalArgumentException`.

new Employee("Ann", 7, "Sales")  -> Ann, 7, Sales
new Employee("Ann", 7)           -> Ann, 7, General
new Employee("Ann")              -> Ann, 0, General
new Employee("  ")               -> IllegalArgumentException

cases.says: The three-argument constructor keeps the name, id and department it is given.
The two-argument constructor sets the department to General.
The one-argument constructor sets the id to 0 and the department to General.
A null or blank name is refused by every constructor, not only the full one.

concepts: Overloaded constructors chain with this(...) to the most specific one, so defaults and checks live in one place.
